messages:
aj: Customer in dedicated env rotated their customer-managed key (CMK) and now their decrypts are failing with 403. they asked us to confirm if our service principal needs a policy change. any quick guidance?

maria: looping in SecEng. do we know exact rotation time and the error from CloudTrail?

aj: customer says rotation at 2026-03-18T21:03:12Z, failures start ~21:05 UTC. pasted error: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-dedicated-svc is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321:key/abcd-ef01`

eli: I'm pulling CloudTrail/KMS logs now. @audit-bot please export events for that key for 2026-03-18T20:50:00Z - 2026-03-18T21:20:00Z

audit-bot: export queued -> s3://redwood-audit/exports/1792104321/key-rotation-20260318.json

eli: quick findings: decrypt attempts from `svcacct-dedicated` IP 54.23.12.8 at 21:05:09 UTC, then retries by `redwood-ops` role at 21:08:23. Key policy change recorded at 21:03:12 — looks like customer replaced policy to only include their IAM principals. our `redwood-dedicated-svc` principal is not present.

sam: that matches my guess — customer rotation likely applied a strict key policy. remediation options: (A) customer adds our role to the key policy; (B) customer issues a short-lived KMS Grant that permits `Decrypt` to our role; (C) customer creates an IAM role in their account we can assume (less preferred).

maria: for least blast radius recommend option B (Grant). Grant is revocable and scoped. we'll provide the exact `create-grant` command so they can run it. also ensure audit trail captures the GrantId.

aj: customer asked if we can apply the change ourselves — they want minimal ops on their side. do we have permission to modify customer key policy?

maria: we do not modify customer-managed CMKs without explicit write consent in contract. we can provide exact commands and can assist in the window while customer runs them, or customer can delegate a short-lived role for us. legal/contract note: any direct modification requires their signed approval.

eli: created internal ticket S-2026-2217 to track. I'll attach the CloudTrail export and initial log snippet.

aj: customer willing to do a 15m maintenance window tomorrow 09:00 UTC. proposed plan: 1) customer runs `create-grant` scoped to our role, 2) we validate decrypts, 3) customer completes rotation confirmation. all actions logged.

sam: command we'll hand to customer:
```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321:key/abcd-ef01 \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-dedicated-svc \
  --operations Decrypt \
  --name "redwood-temp-rot-grant"
```
Include `--constraints` if they want to limit to a specific encryption context. capture `GrantId` output and send to us.

maria: also request from customer: export of `GenerateDataKey` and `Decrypt` events for last 30 days for risk assessment, and a list of principals that rotated the key. we'll include that in the post-incident notes.

aj: I've sent the command and docs. customer asked whether this is an indication of compromise — they checked and only their rotation action shows in Console. no anomalous principals.

eli: good. after we have the Grant, we'll run a small end-to-end test: call our decrypt path in staging and then in prod dedicated tenant. capture results and CloudTrail events.

maria: follow-up actions: - S-2026-2217 to track policy/grant change - attach audit export - schedule 48h postmortem with customer + privacy + support - add runbook entry in SecPlaybook about CMK rotation checks for dedicated envs

aj: customer accepted 09:00 UTC window, I'll coordinate. i'll update ticket with GrantId and result.

eli: once the change is done, please also upload the `create-grant` stdout (redact ARNs if needed) to the ticket so we have proof of action.

maria: no blockers from SecEng. ensure we do not retain customer keys or key material.

aj: will confirm. closing loop with customer until the maintenance window. :thumbsup:

sam: postmortem note: consider adding an automated pre-rotation check that validates our service principal presence in CMK policy and alerts the customer if missing. low-effort but prevents this class of breakage.

maria: agreed — add to backlog after incident is closed.

aj: thanks everyone, will report back after the window.
